# Marimo Studio 0.1.0

Marimo Studio keeps one saved Marimo notebook as the analytical model and lets
you build a named web view for each job. The notebook owns data access, Python
computation, controls, and reusable results. Each view owns its frontend source,
layout, wording, and browser interaction.

Create a first view and open it beside the notebook:

```console
uvx --from marimo-studio==0.1.0 marimo-studio view create dashboard --target analysis.py
uvx --with marimo-studio==0.1.0 marimo edit analysis.py --sandbox
```

Choose **Develop** to work with Notebook, Source, and Preview in one session.

## What ships

- Named view projects backed by browser-native HTML, React, Reveal.js, Svelte,
  or an installed view provider. Vanilla views can keep CSS and JavaScript
  inline or reference local files directly.
- `<marimo-cell>`, `<marimo-output>`, and `mo-value` projections that place
  complete cells, rendered Python objects, and browser values in custom
  frontend source.
- Immutable build artifacts with source-located diagnostics. A failed build
  keeps the last successful view available.
- Python Server and browser WebAssembly runtimes with live delivery through
  `marimo run`. WebAssembly views can also be exported as static directories
  for HTTP hosting.
- Revision-safe Source editing plus Python and CLI authoring contracts for
  coding agents to inspect, edit, build, show, and validate the same rendered
  view a person sees.
- Exact-origin allowlisting for [embedding the Studio edit
  workspace](https://marimo-team.github.io/marimo-studio/guide/deploy#embed-the-studio-edit-workspace).
  Same-origin framing remains the default, and Marimo authentication remains
  required.
- Nine live views backed by three notebooks, with source and guided
  documentation for reports, explorers, maps, monitors, model reviews, stories,
  and presentations.

## Upgrade from 0.0.6

Marimo Studio 0.1.0 begins the first documented compatibility line. Existing
0.0.6 views need a `view.toml` manifest before Studio can discover them. CLI
automation moves to the `notebook`, `view`, `status`, and `validate` commands,
and Python authoring moves to `marimo_studio.authoring` or
`marimo_studio.agent`.

Follow the [0.0.6 upgrade
table](https://marimo-team.github.io/marimo-studio/reference/compatibility#upgrade-from-006)
before opening an existing workspace with 0.1.0.

## Compatibility

Marimo Studio 0.1.0 supports Python 3.10 through 3.14 and Marimo 0.24.0. React,
Reveal.js, and Svelte authoring use the optional Deno 2.9.5 dependency. Browser
acceptance targets current Chromium on Linux and Windows.

Installed view providers execute trusted Python and child commands with the
current user's permissions. Review provider packages and dependencies before
using them in an environment with credentials or private notebook source.

Read the [documentation](https://marimo-team.github.io/marimo-studio/),
[compatibility and support policy](https://marimo-team.github.io/marimo-studio/reference/compatibility),
and [troubleshooting guide](https://marimo-team.github.io/marimo-studio/guide/troubleshooting).
